description:
MEASURED AND FIXED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop.

SYMPTOM. OPCPFluidArray::set_mass_flowrate was inert storage: it wrote the 'mass_flowrate' field, which step() never reads. The only way to impose flow was a fixed inlet VELOCITY, so a caller had to convert with an assumed density -- and the imposed flow then came out as mdot_actual = (rho_solved/rho_assumed) * mdot_target, drifting by exactly the density error. Reported downstream as a 1.33 MW imbalance between the two sides of an otherwise-converged counter-flow heat exchanger.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, seed and inlet 300 K, PISO 2 correctors, dt 2e-4 s, 2000 steps, target mdot = 1.0 g/s; actual flow read from the solved boundary face flux phi):
  velocity from the CORRECT density rho(300 K, 1 bar) = 1.12328 kg/m3 -> 9.999122e-4 kg/s  (-0.0088 %)
  velocity from a DESIGN-POINT density rho(600 K, 1 bar) = 0.56130 kg/m3 -> 2.000597e-3 kg/s  (+100.06 %)
  prescribed mass-flow inlet -> 1.000000000000e-3 kg/s  (relative error exactly 0.0)

FIX. A correct fix IS in reach and is the standard one -- this is OpenFOAM's flowRateInletVelocity BC (src/finiteVolume/fields/fvPatchFields/derived/flowRateInletVelocity/). New Option<MassRate> field 'inlet_mass_flowrate'; each pressure corrector of step() re-derives u_in = mdot/(rho_inlet*A_inlet) from the CURRENT interpolated inlet-FACE density -- the same rho_f value that then multiplies it to build the boundary mass flux -- so the imposed flux is exactly -mdot by construction, independent of how the density evolves. self.u.boundary and step()'s captured u_bcs template are updated together so the momentum predictor and the post-solve correct_bcs_vec re-stamps agree.

NEW PUBLIC API (all additive; NO version bump, NO signature change):
  set_inlet_mass_flowrate / get_inlet_mass_flowrate / clear_inlet_mass_flowrate
  get_inlet_mass_flowrate_actual / get_outlet_mass_flowrate_actual  (diagnostics read off phi)
  set_inlet_velocity now clears a prescribed mass-flow inlet (they prescribe the same patch)
  new pub field OPCPFluidArray::inlet_mass_flowrate -- technically semver-breaking for anyone constructing the struct by literal, which nothing in the workspace does.
set_mass_flowrate is left as bookkeeping, with its doc comment now saying so plainly and pointing at the real BC.

REGRESSION TESTS:
  lateral_coupling::tests::mass_flow_inlet_imposes_the_prescribed_flowrate  (also asserts the assumed-density route is visibly wrong, so the test cannot pass by the two routes coinciding)
  lateral_coupling::tests::mass_flow_inlet_closes_the_steady_energy_balance  (200 W source: mdot*(h_out-h_in) = 200.0574 W, +0.03 %, T_out 491.29 K)
  lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_velocity_and_mass_flow_bcs_are_mutually_exclusive

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables' TampinesSteamArray has the identical inert set_mass_flowrate; the same fix transplants directly.
title: OPCPFluidArray: set_mass_flowrate never entered the solution -- added a real flow-rate inlet BC (FIXED)

description: s38. A SEPARATE tab/area exposing real Git concepts: status/diff/history, branches, remotes, fetch/pull/push. Use gitoxide for guaranteed LOCAL operations. Use the SYSTEM git binary for remote/network operations and authentication -- do NOT depend on gitoxide remotes. Kovan must remain fully functional without system Git; only remote operations become unavailable.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented: src/advanced_git.rs + digitiser/gui/desktop/advanced_git_view.rs (new Advanced Git tab). Strict local/remote split per s38: status/local_branches/history are gix-backed, REUSING crate::repository::status and kovan_discovery::git::GitProvider (not a second implementation of either) -- local_branches() is the one genuinely new gix call (repo.references()?.local_branches()). fetch/pull/push/list_remotes shell out to the SYSTEM git binary via std::process::Command, explicitly NOT kovan_discovery::GixCliBackend despite the tempting name match -- confirmed by reading its source that it wraps the gix CLI (a different tool) and every GitBackend method on it is currently a stub returning Unsupported; using it for remote ops would have been silently wrong. system_git_available() lets Kovan report 'remote operations unavailable' cleanly rather than hang/panic when git is missing (s38's own requirement). Tests exercise fetch/pull/push for real, against a local --bare repo standing in for a remote -- no network access needed or used.

title: kovan redesign 20: Advanced Git tab + system-git remote layer

description: Replace the single-Gaussian (central-limit) diffusion step, which overshoots the thin buffer layer (sqrt(2*D*dt) >= layer thickness at second-scale dt) and forces slow Fourier sub-timestepping, with a timestep-free Walk-on-Spheres / Green's-function first-passage random walk. Adds interface transmission/reflection (linear-D rule, verified vs uniform-density equilibrium), decay+transmutation depletion (competing clocks, no Bateman matrix), rayon parallel ensembles, an Android-gated wgpu compute scaffold, and a real-time egui demonstrator. Branch claude/boon-lay-branch-m8wmns, commits f24a53f..f47c55d. 167 lib tests green; Android --all-targets clean.
title: boon-lay: Walk-on-Spheres first-passage diffusion engine — fixes buffer-CLT overshoot, adds interface physics, depletion, rayon/wgpu acceleration, real-time viz

description:
Parent: op-841p. Rung 1 is the reference every other rung is validated against, so its credibility is the pipeline's credibility.

TARGET SEQUENCE, cheapest first, each with a published number to hit:
1a. TRISO grain unit cell, infinite medium. DONE as a code exercise: crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs (see comment on this bead for the measured numbers). Free-gas thermal scattering, so NOT a physics result.
1b. Infinite pebble-bed lattice k_inf vs Serpent 1.6321 / HCP 1.6416 (Tantillo et al. 2020, Nucl. Eng. Des. 362, 110603, PROPRIETARY tier - cite, do not re-host).
1c. BCC fuel + graphite ball lattice k_inf vs MCNP5 1.77078 +/- 0.00008 (Wang et al. 2014, config b, PROPRIETARY tier).
1d. B1 detailed core k_eff at the measured 16890-ball / 123.06 cm loading vs MCNP5 1.01620 +/- 0.00014 (Wang et al. 2014, config c).

Steps 1a-1c are reachable with the existing reflective-cube driver run_keff_delta. Step 1d needs run_keff_csg plus a bed model.

EVERY REPORTED k MUST CARRY: sigma, particles per generation, inactive and active generation counts, RNG seed, cross-section library and version, fidelity tier (from_core LOW vs from_endf HIGH), and the thermal-scattering treatment. A k_eff without sigma and without data provenance is not a result.

STATE WHICH PROBLEM: B1-as-defined (helium, 20 C, dummy balls 1.73 g/cm3 and 1.3 ppm boron) or B1-as-measured (humid air 0.1013 MPa at 15 C, water-vapour density 2.57e-5 g/cm3, dummy balls 1.84 g/cm3 and 0.125 ppm). They differ by about +1000 pcm - larger than the published code-to-code spread of 683 +/- 22 pcm. Conflating them invalidates the comparison against the measured 123.06 cm.

Benchmark specification is typed data at crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/neutronics.rs. Scoping: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 4.1.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
RUNG 1 STEP 1a COMPLETED as a code exercise, 2026-08-11. crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs.

PROBLEM: HTR-10 fuel-zone infinite medium, run twice - kernels resolved explicitly as randomly packed spheres, then the same nuclide inventory homogenised. Atom densities straight from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 Table 4-38 (OPEN tier, part 2 line 1101). Kernel volume fraction of the fuelled zone = 8335 * (0.025/2.5)^3 = 8.335e-3.

MEASURED (main run, 400 particles/generation, 10 inactive + 40 active, RNG seed 1, packing seed 20260811, 1018 kernels of r = 0.025 cm in a reflective cube of half-width 1 cm, realized packing fraction 0.008328, T = 293.15 K, delta tracking with a bin-maximum bounding majorant):
  heterogeneous k_inf = 1.57269 +/- 0.00877
  homogenised   k_inf = 1.45189 +/- 0.00820
  delta k = -12081 +/- 1201 pcm; delta rho = -5291 +/- 526 pcm; 10.1 sigma
A smoke run at 200/8/25 gave 1.60870 +/- 0.02031 and 1.47273 +/- 0.01489, agreeing with the main run to 1.6 sigma on the heterogeneous case.

SIGN IS A PHYSICS CHECK AND IT PASSES: resolving the kernels depresses the flux inside each lump at the U-238 resonance energies, so fewer resonance absorptions per U-238 atom and k rises; homogenising removes the depression so it must come out lower. It does.

THIS IS NOT A PHYSICS RESULT AND NOT AN HTR-10 CRITICALITY RESULT:
- Thermal scattering is FREE GAS. Graphite S(alpha,beta) does not reach the transport path (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs:24-26). On a graphite-moderated thermal system this alone disqualifies the absolute number.
- It is a fuel-zone infinite medium - no shell, no dummy ball, no bed, no reflector, no leakage. NO published HTR-10 value corresponds to this problem, so the absolute k_inf cannot be compared to the literature at all.
- TRISO coatings unresolved (op-6tz.35). LOW fidelity tier (flat nu-bar, Watt chi stand-in, ~+500 pcm on Godiva). k_std is a generation-batch SEM with no inter-generation correlation correction. op-rbo and op-jis inherited.
- The delta k is NOT comparable to Wang et al.'s unit-cell biases: theirs are multigroup XS PROCESSING biases against a CE reference on the full model and run the other way (+2820 pcm for INFHOMMEDIUM). This is a CE GEOMETRIC effect on a different problem.

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH: the rung-1 chain runs end to end on this reactor's real materials, reproducibly from a stated seed, with a correctly signed self-shielding effect.

COST WARNING for step 1d: thermal neutrons in graphite scatter hundreds of times per history. The 400/10/40 run took roughly 20 minutes for 40,000 histories. Budget compute accordingly.

Full write-up: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 11.

title: HTR-10 rung 1: pebble-bed Monte Carlo reference k_eff, with sigma and stated data provenance

description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 07:1x (filed outside active hours; no code work done).

Add a toggle in the simulator GUI to switch temperature readouts between degrees Celsius and Kelvin.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT (important -- do not get this wrong):
- This is a DISPLAY-LAYER concern only. Internal state stays uom-typed (ThermodynamicTemperature) and is never converted to a bare f64 'current display unit'. The toggle selects which uom accessor is called at render time (get::<degree_celsius>() vs get::<kelvin>()), nothing more.
- Do NOT introduce a units field into the physics/plant state, and do NOT let the display unit reach any correlation, controller, or solver input. A display toggle that leaks into the model is exactly the silent unit error the uom typing exists to prevent.
- Label every readout with its unit; the toggle changes the label as well as the number.

SCOPE QUESTION for the maintainer: which simulator(s)?
- htgr_sim_v1 specifically, or
- all the egui simulators in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (fhr_sim_v2, CIET, etc.)?
If it is more than one, the toggle belongs as a shared widget/state in the digital-twin engine rather than being copy-pasted per example -- check what already exists there before adding it (search-before-building rule).

Also confirm: temperature only, or a general unit-preference system (pressure bar/MPa/psi, flow kg/s vs L/min)? Scoping it as temperature-only now is fine, but the shared-widget decision above depends on the answer.

Related: op-szmi.5 (finish the htgr_sim_v1 GUI to CIET v2 standard).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
SCOPE ANSWERED by maintainer, 2026-08-13: htgr_sim_v1 ONLY.

So the toggle lives in the htgr_sim_v1 GUI, not as a shared digital-twin-engine widget. Do not refactor the other simulators (fhr_sim_v2, CIET) for this.

Still worth a quick look at what the engine already provides before hand-rolling a widget -- if a temperature-formatting helper already exists there, use it; just do not promote this into a cross-simulator feature.

Remaining open question (unchanged): temperature only, or other units too? Proceeding as temperature-only unless told otherwise.

title: Simulator GUI: user-toggleable temperature display units (degC / K)

Quality bar: look derives from the component's real dimensions and live state, not from arbitrary screen coordinates; document units, valid ranges and what drives what in the /// doc comment; add tests; and per the workspace V&V rule state BOTH methodology and measured results where anything is checked against a reference. Do not fabricate a value to render -- an unpopulated component must be visibly distinct from a cold one (PipeVisual's neutral-grey empty case is the precedent).
